evidence: Bounded installer defect, not a failure of the measured normal launch: frozen task/solution/solve.sh:15-27 scans every /proc process and throws on every error other than ENOENT/ESRCH, before the copy at line 33. In an isolated fresh container with neither /app/server.js nor /app/app.db, an unrelated nobody-owned sleep process causes exit 1: "EACCES: permission denied, readlink /proc/8/fd/0"; server.js remains absent. Stopping only that sleeper makes the unchanged installer exit 0 and install server.js. This adds an undocumented ability-to-read-every-process precondition to workbook row 19's installer promise and instruction.md:9,11 / integration.md:3-10's self-contained /app launch contract; it is not necessary to protect a database that does not exist. The probe is a deliberately constructed, otherwise permissible Linux process condition, not an observed failure of the ordinary hosted Oracle setup. Independent raw record: per-row-review/evidence/19/run.json identifies command, network-none disposable container, exact image sha256:fd5a522e1caa5692f9e3ece733b3f60ea79b20b1cf4b4aaf75bd99f5ccce8c27 and artifacts; install-isolation-result.json SHA256 991d685082c7dcd8f22d6324749fa21d578617ab98dce472b2ea0be5b9d598ff; tested solve.sh SHA256 3bf863a5703a9c7297986ca72a6300b47780546531e966b3a7386982dc852741. Positive evidence is preserved: bash -n passed and solve.sh is LF-only, copies only into /app, and contains no pkill, NODE_ENV=production or package install. db.js:13-28 honors DB_PATH and reads the co-located matching seed; db.js:122-179 seeds transactionally once. bootstrap.js:20-24 answers health independently of database work and :43-45 honors PORT on 0.0.0.0 in the same Node process. The hash-verified existing lifecycle driver starts the current 13-file golden as uid 65534 from /tests with sanitized env, then the actual shared restart MCP replaces PID 21 with PID 97 and retains the saved requisition. Its results.json SHA256 is 52b5ba96bded2e133fe4ec16117c150d46673f70ce31284169193f478c73e9f9; verification-extra.json binds all 37 current task files. Eight cited index artifact hashes, every lifecycle app hash, and all task source hashes were independently checked in evidence/19/hash-verification.json. The internal workbook no-network/no-install wording is superseded by the public row and skill; no network defect is alleged. These are finite installer/runtime observations, not private deterministic checker execution, full configured judge completion, or an Oracle/model score.
counterexample: Confirmed conforming-runtime alternative that the installer falsely rejects: an otherwise fresh permitted Linux container has one unrelated uid-65534 sleep 30 process, no app server and no database. The installer should be able to copy the static application, but its global /proc scan fails before doing so. A conforming installer can skip database-inactivity inspection when the database and its journals are all absent while retaining conservative protection for an existing database. Plausible broken-app escape considered (reasoning only): an app that deletes/reseeds its database at every node startup would pass a fresh install and health check, but is rejected by the actual lifecycle positive-control/create/restart/identical-readback probe; the current app retains that saved record.
suggested_fix: Skip the inactivity scan for a genuinely absent database and journals, or use a database-scoped ownership/locking mechanism; preserve refusal when an existing database may be active and add the unrelated-process fresh-install control.
